description: P1-6 performance acceptance contract acceptance_v2 (decision D-14; supersedes acceptance_v1 for every real acceptance, Phase 1 xhigh acceptance review findings 1 and 2, window re-declared after the follow-up review's finding 1 before any candidate was judged). Same schema, harness, judge, reference variant, seeds, physics plan, thresholds (except primary_pairs_above_1) and evaluator file set as acceptance_v1; the G9 speed gate times the s512 tool-material contact and cutting phase (control steps 229-400 of the replay from reset) instead of the pre-contact approach (acceptance_v1: steps 21-120 at N=8/16), with fewer N and pairs to fit the budget. Frozen at the commit that merges it into main (tests/test_acceptance_frozen.py pins its sha256); any change after that is acceptance_v3.

design.window: G9 replays s512 from reset and times control steps 229-400 (warmup_steps 228, steps 172) at every N; there is no steps_by_num_envs, every N times the same steps. Two counters, from the WP-17 Native s512 per-step material statistics (privileged_diagnostics.material_contact_statistics in actions.jsonl) and the P1-6 R0 smoke_003 G6 dumps: stats slot 1 = tool-material contacts (handle, pads, edge obstacles against particles), non-zero at steps 229-366 (101 non-zero steps, gaps 237-256 and 259-273, total 308,600); stats slot 4 = particle-particle (cut-face) contacts, non-zero at steps 315-364 (49 steps, total 152,455 in the replay dumps, identical ranges for frozen_v1 and alias_free_v1 and in the GPU window check). Labelling (cutting): 0 at step 250, 1,978 at 260, 37,958 from step 380. The window 229-400 therefore times all 101 tool-contact steps, all 49 particle-contact steps and all labelling (0 -> 37,958), plus 34 post-contact steps (367-400); the untimed warm-up 1-228 is the approach only. Step 229 is the first Native tool-contact step, so W = 228 is the largest warm-up that loses none of it. s15 (held out, not timed): tool contact 229-516, particle contact 321-842, labels until 530. G9:window gates tool-contact steps (slot 1) and new labels on the G6/G7 episode dumps (the harness dumps slot 1 as tool_contacts since this declaration): minimums 80 of 101 tool-contact steps and 30,000 of 37,958 labels (about 20 % margin each, set from the Native data before the GPU re-check); particle contacts are reported, not gated. The cutting-onset steps 255-258 and 274-275 showed 2-3.7x step walls in the first (SHARED_GPU) check; their cause is not established and they are now timed.
design.statistics: Kept from acceptance_v1: ABBA pairs in one lock hold per N on the same GPU, the caller's outer clock, N=16 primary (median >= 1.05 and every pair > 1.0), every-N floor (median >= 0.97), clock tolerance 5 %. Changed for the budget: pairs 5 -> 3 (order BCCBBC) and N {1, 8, 16} -> {1, 16}. This is a trade-off, not stricter than v1 as a whole: only the sign-test part is stricter (3 of 3 pairs, false-accept 1/8 under no change, v1 4 of 5 = 3/16), and with the 1.05 median floor both false-accept rates are about 0 for a neutral candidate; with pair noise sigma <= 0.02 (log ratio) v2 roughly doubles the near-threshold errors in both directions, with sigma >= 0.03 it loses power (a true 1.10 is rejected about 14 % of the time at sigma 0.05, v1 about 5 %); the N=1 floor rests on 3 pairs of 172 timed steps (v1: 5 pairs of 300); N=8 and every N other than 1 and 16 is not gated. N=8 is dropped rather than N=1 because N=8 and N=16 are both in the baseline's saturated regime (aggregate env-steps/s flat from N=4) and N=1 is the only unsaturated point (9.6 % of G9 GPU time). Exclusive repeats show sigma about 0.006, where these effects are negligible: run acceptances on an EXCLUSIVE_GPU where possible.
design.budget: GPU time only. Estimated from the EXCLUSIVE_GPU workload-A rows of alias_free_v1 (the reference variant; exclusive_001 pre-contact per-step medians N=1 0.0978 s, N=8 0.5709 s, N=16 1.1799 s; per-process overhead 13.0-14.8 s): a G9 run is 400 replay steps whatever the W/K split: N=1 52 s, N=16 487 s; G9 = 6 x 539 s = 53.9 min (N=1 9.6 %); physics plan (unchanged from v1): G6 6 x 261 s = 26.1 min, G7 2 x 362 s = 12.1 min, G4 4 x 57 s = 3.8 min, G8 2 x 75 s = 2.5 min = 44.5 min; one acceptance 98.4 GPU-min = 1.64 GPU-h exclusive. Contact-phase revision from the first window check (one SHARED_GPU N=2 episode run of alias_free_v1: mean step wall over steps 1-400 = 1.061 x the approach mean; contact-phase median 1.33 x the approach median; the factor at N=16 is unmeasured): about 1.75 GPU-h exclusive per acceptance, within 2.5 h up to about x1.43 co-tenant slowdown; largest lock hold (G9 N=16) about 52 min exclusive, <= 90 min up to about x1.73. Not in the GPU time: the G1/G2 CPU suites (cpu_tests.args tests, 50-53 min per side on the RCS host), which the external caller runs in parallel with the GPU blocks and the local runner runs one side after the other. Rejected: the v1 statistics with a contact window (5 pairs, N 1/8/16) = 130 min of G9 (N=16 hold 81 min exclusive) and 2.9 GPU-h per acceptance; 3 pairs with N 1/8/16 = 78 min of G9 and 2.04 GPU-h. Under heavy co-tenancy (smoke_003: x2.2) one acceptance exceeds 2.5 h and its absolute rows are SHARED_GPU; the caller's GPU admission should wait instead.

thresholds.reset_p95_rule: G9:<n>:reset on the per-side medians of reset p95 over all ABBA processes at N. Both sides EXCLUSIVE_GPU: FAIL if C > reset_p95_ratio_max x B + reset_p95_slack_ms. Either side SHARED_GPU (or UNKNOWN): PASS if C <= ratio x B + reset_p95_slack_ms; WARN shared_gpu_reset_bimodality (verdict.warnings, not a failure) if C <= ratio x B + reset_p95_shared_slack_ms; FAIL above that. Reason: on a shared GPU each process settles in a ~1 ms or ~7 ms reset mode independent of the variant (smoke_001: B 1.7 ms vs C 7.1 ms at N=1, reversed at N=2).
thresholds.candidate_reported: VRAM peak (nvidia-smi per-process samples of the process tree, allocator fallback), reset p95 and the per-step walls of performance.phases are measured inside the process under test (candidate-reported, not independently verified); only env-steps/s has the caller's outer clock
thresholds.rules: G9 per N: median over the ABBA pairs of candidate/baseline outer-clock env-steps/s; primary N median >= primary_median_min with >= primary_pairs_above_1 pairs > 1.0; every N median >= all_median_min; max VRAM peak C <= vram_ratio_max x max B + vram_slack_mib; median reset p95 per reset_p95_rule; every G9 run |inner/outer - 1| <= clock_tolerance; G9:window: in every episode dump of the window_check plans for the G9 seeds (both sides, every repeat) the G9 window holds >= min_tool_contact_steps steps with non-zero tool-material contacts (stats slot 1, dumped as tool_contacts) and >= min_new_labels new labelled particles (candidate below while the baseline meets it: FAIL; the baseline below: BLOCKED); particle-particle contacts (slot 4) are reported only; performance.phases: per-phase median step walls per side and their ratio, descriptive only

physics.position_rule: full episodes: the final maximum position difference vs Native is compared with the band file's high value per seed (or the reference variant's own value for that seed in the same acceptance, whichever is larger). mode descriptive: a WARN in verdict.warnings and the gate values, never a gate result; mode gate: a PHYSICS check. band v2 is the pre-declared 10-replay one-sided 99 % log-normal bound; it stays descriptive in acceptance_v2.
physics.contact_total_rel_tol_note: Kept at 0.02 (acceptance_v1 raised it from 0.01 after P1-6 R0 smoke_003, before any baseline): frozen_v1 vs alias_free_v1 s15 contact totals differ by 0.51 % (s512 0.03 %), so 0.01 left only a 2x margin for a known-good change, and G7 has one baseline run per acceptance (no spread term).
physics.rules: episodes (hard gates): final codes = Native, labelled counts = Native, sample invariants (finite, digits <= 2, no digit rewrites, invalid_reason 0), frozen TRIM evaluator PASS on 2 frames and on the Native sample series, per-env contact total within max(contact_total_rel_tol, 2 x baseline spread) of the baseline median; position band per position_band.mode; samestate: per recorded sample identical non-zero impulse sets (both reruns) and stats[4], impulse max relative difference <= impulse_rel_tol; short replay final codes equal, positions within replay_position_tol_m, contact totals within contact_total_rel_tol; a candidate failure where the baseline fails the same check for the same seed is BLOCKED
